It's only reproducible in 4.4+ as the API doesn't exist in 4.3. The method was introduced in 4.4.dev7 with #100110 and that version crashes too.

Spamming this function in `_process` definitely doesn't sound like a good idea and a supported use case, but it shouldn't crash.

CC @DarioSamo @clayjohn

@akien-mga I'm working on NDI Output for Godot, so I need the texture every frame. ~~Is there a better place to call it from? Like on a draw notification/signal?~~ Now that you mention it, calling it every process doesn't make sense. The RenderingServer emits `frame_post_draw`. That'd be a better time to call the function.

This could be unrelated, but let's say I call `RD::texture_get_data_async` to request texture data, but in the meantime the Object/Node that owns the method pointed to by the Callable gets freed / deconstructed. Would that cause a crash? I think that's what I'm seeing here now that I'm calling it on `RenderingServer::frame_post_draw` instead of on every process.

> This could be unrelated, but let's say I call `RD::texture_get_data_async` to request texture data, but in the meantime the Object/Node that owns the method pointed to by the Callable gets freed / deconstructed. Would that cause a crash? I think that's what I'm seeing here now that I'm calling it on `RenderingServer::frame_post_draw` instead of on every process.

That'd likely lead to a crash yes. You're responsible for the lifetime of your objects and you shouldn't destroy them until the callback comes back.

You could easily work around that by handing off that responsibility to an object that always lives and is in charge of redirecting the data to the object.

That said, I'll still investigate the original stack trace to see if it can be reproduced in the situation that was mentioned in the OP first.

This PR should fix it. This project exposed a bug in the method's implementation.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102454

A word of warning however: this happened because the code you've posted requires so much memory to be downloaded that it's immediately triggering the frame to be processed and flushed. Absolutely no frame queuing can happen in this situation, which will very much limit the performance of the engine. Dealing with this requires for the user to adjust their project settings as described here.

https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_renderingdevice.html#class-renderingdevice-method-texture-get-data-async

The crash was merely because the engine was not handling the fallback under the stress of this situation properly.

Thanks for the warning. The the callback method being freed is not related to this issue then. 

> You could easily work around that by handing off that responsibility to an object that always lives and is in charge of redirecting the data to the object.

I implemented a "ViewportTextureRouter" that receives the callback and lives as a Singleton until the GDExtension gets unloaded. That just moved the crash from happening when closing the scene to happening when unloading the GDExtension.

Unrelated though, so I'll try to make an MRP with GDScript and create a new issue. Thanks for your work here!
Can confirm, MRP doesn't crash with https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/102454
